periods.label: 2020-21 international signing period
periods.notes: Moved for financial reasons during the pandemic: it was due to open July 2, 2020 and opened Jan 15, 2021 instead, running to Dec 15, 2021 at 5 pm ET. This was the first calendar-year window. Eligibility was unchanged (players turning 16 by Aug 31, 2020), and pool slots could not be traded in 2020 or 2021. There is no separate '2021' period: the 2020-21 period covers calendar 2021.

periods.label: 2022 international signing period (officially styled '2021-22')
periods.notes: MLB and MLBTR call this the '2021-22' period. It opened Jan 15, 2022 during the MLB lockout (Dec 2, 2021 - Mar 10, 2022), which did not stop minor-league international signings. The 2022-2026 CBA, ratified March 2022, was in force for most of the period. Pool size was set under the prior system, and the international-draft question stayed open until July 25, 2022. Calling the rules_era CBA_2017_2021 is a judgment call; it could also be classed as CBA_2022_2026.

rules_eras.label: 2012-2016 CBA: soft-capped bonus pools with overage tax and penalties
rules_eras.summary: Each club got an international bonus pool, with a base amount plus an allotment set by reverse prior-season record. Bonuses of $10K or less were exempt, as were players 23+ with 5+ years in a foreign pro league. Exceeding the pool brought a tiered tax plus later limits. The original 2012-13 table (FanGraphs) ran from a 75% tax at 0-5% over up to a 100% tax plus a one-period $250K per-player cap at 15%+. Later sources (SBD Jan 2014; MLB.com 2015) describe the top tier as 100% tax and no bonus over $300K for the next two periods. MLB.com (2015) gives the 0-5% tier as a 100% tax, which conflicts with FanGraphs' 75%. The tier details changed during the CBA and should be confirmed against the CBA text. These rules covered the 2012-13 through 2016-17 periods.

rules_eras.label: 2017-2021 CBA: hard-capped bonus pools
rules_eras.effective_to: 2021-12-01 (CBA expiry; the 2021-22 period opened Jan 15, 2022 during the lockout)
rules_eras.summary: The CBA agreed Dec 2016 adopted no international draft. Pools became hard caps starting in 2017-18: most clubs got $4.75M, and some got $5.25M or $5.75M by competitive-balance tier. The exemption threshold rose to age 25 with 6 years in a foreign pro league (from 23 and 5). Clubs could trade for added pool space up to 75% of their original pool in 2017-18 and 2018-19, then 60%. Clubs already penalized under the old rules served out those penalties. During COVID, the 2019-20 period was extended to Oct 15, 2020, the 2020-21 period moved to Jan 15 - Dec 15, 2021, and pool trades were barred in 2020-21.

rules_eras.label: 2022-2026 CBA: hard-capped pools continue, calendar-year periods, international draft not adopted
rules_eras.summary: The March 10, 2022 lockout settlement set a July 25, 2022 deadline for an international draft and linked it to dropping qualifying-offer draft-pick compensation. The MLBPA rejected MLB's final offer on July 25, 2022, so hard-capped international free agency and the QO system both continued. Per a side letter, the 2022-23 pool total stayed at $167M and then grows with industry revenue. Periods run Jan 15 - Dec 15 and clubs may trade for up to 60% of their original pool. The CBA expires Dec 1, 2026. In June 2026 talks MLB again proposed an international draft ($200M hard pool, minimum age 18); as of the sources found, nothing was agreed and the 2026 process was unaffected.
